doc: Calling the Harvest (slug harvest-almanac) - slot 5 of the expert-everyday-2 batch (THR-1679).

plotHookRolled: hook.trial_by_combat, hook.siege_and_hold, hook.natural_disaster
plotHookTaken: hook.natural_disaster - the storm is the disaster, kept at village scale; Hubris vs. Humility
is the Proud/Humble opposition the dice rolled.
Mechanical design block:
Crux            A village asks {actor} to name the day its harvest starts, and a storm is coming.
Shape           Single Test, one step, Star 0.64 (steep), fail_action.
Rolled dice     p3 opportunity - opposition own trait (Proud / Judgemental) - disposition friendly -
role suspect or cause - scale personal.
Consequence     (THR-1145) drive + movement, no swap. Success half: reputation_with $here +0.06,
agent_relocation nearest_settlement (travel; a lean that lapses), assign_ambition
ambition_great_work. Failure half: reputation_with $here -0.06, plant_compulsion
assist 0.5 for 72 ticks.
Cool failure    Nobody is hurt, jailed or branded: a lost crop and a lost name.
Systems quota   cast (elder) + rewards (assign_ambition) + reputation = three, the floor.
Trait hooks     Proud -0.05 (+ Stoke Their Pride, Delta 0.05, cancels it exactly), Judgemental -0.04,
Humble +0.04.
Deal            count 5 (common-option starvation measured at count 4: 6 of 132 god shapes).
Fiction note    The almanac survives only in the concept art; the ambition is builder-civic and no
chip claims an almanac (Pass 3b fold).
Critic loop: editorial PASS WITH REVISIONS, systems READY WITH CAVEATS, package PASS.

template.name: Calling the Harvest

openings.rural: {actor} arrives at {location} at the end of summer.

steps.narrativeTemplate:
The barley is nearly ripe. The stars say it needs a few more days to fill, but a storm is building in the west and may not give them.

{cast:elder}, the village elder, asks {actor} to read the sky and name the day the harvest starts. Every household cuts on that one word. Villages all down the valley send for a reader who gets that call right.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: {actor} judged the storm would not wait, and named the next morning.
steps.successAfterimage: {actor} weighed the stars against the storm, and named a day early enough.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: {actor} named a day, then brought it forward at the last hour.
steps.failureAfterimage: {actor} held to the stars and named a day too late.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: {actor} kept the stars' day, even when the wind turned.

effects.narrativeHook: They called the harvest right, and mean to build something the whole valley can lean on.
They called the harvest wrong, and they mean to help bring in what is left.

nudges.name: Hasten The Signs
nudges.effectLine: Make the warnings of a coming change show early, so there is more to read before the choice.

bandProse.critical_success: The swallows flew low a day early, and {actor} read the storm in them at once.
bandProse.success: The warnings came a day early, and {actor} had weighed every one before the call.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The warnings came early enough for {actor} to change the day, though not for every field.
bandProse.near_miss: The warnings came early, but they did not agree, and {actor} had to guess between them.
bandProse.failure: The warnings came early, and {actor} took them for a passing shower.
bandProse.critical_failure: The warnings came early and loud, and {actor} named a later day all the same.

nudges.name: Stoke Their Pride
nudges.effectLine: Make every murmur of doubt rankle, so they go over the work again to prove it right.

bandProse.success: Every murmur sent {actor} back to the sky, and the second reading caught the storm.
bandProse.success_at_cost: {actor} went back to the stars again and again to prove the doubters wrong, and did not sleep.
bandProse.failure: {actor} checked the stars again to prove the doubters wrong, and saw only the day already named.
bandProse.critical_failure: Every murmur made {actor} surer, and {actor} would not hear another word about the storm.

traitVariants.factorLine: Being Proud, they will not easily take back a day once named.
Being Judgemental, they take every sign as proof of their first reading.
Being Humble, they will change the day if the storm says so.

template.description: A one-step Star test for an expert in a village: the elder asks a star-reader to name the day the harvest starts, with a storm coming. A right call raises their standing, sends them on the road to the nearest settlement and gives them the Build a Great Work ambition; a wrong one costs their standing and leaves them helping others for a while. Proud and Judgemental readers find it harder to give up the stars' day.
